task.description: BACKEND SCOPE ONLY for this run (the frontend NonSkippableApprovalGate.tsx surfacing piece is deliberately split out as ISS-0767, letflow-queue task 767 -- do not design frontend changes here). Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0732-20260921/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnosis.json's result.summary in full -- it is ISSUE-FIXER's complete first-hand diagnosis, including the exact fix shape it recommends, the exact @spec/return-shape of get_latest_assertion_run/2, and the exact gate condition (assertions_failed == 0) promotions.ex's moduledoc already documents for R8. Produce a gate-approved design artefact (lib/letflow/design/ per this repo's own convention, e.g. lib/letflow/design/iss0732-promotion-apply-assertion-gate.md) for a NEW precondition in Letflow.Definitions.Promotion.apply_review/4's `with` chain (lib/letflow/definitions/promotion.ex), inserted after verify_approved/1 and before do_apply_review/3 is called, that: (1) calls Letflow.Definitions.get_latest_assertion_run(review.id, opts); (2) on {:error, :not_found}, short-circuits with a new, DISTINCT apply_review_error() reason (do not reuse :invalid_transition -- callers/tests/the frontend need to distinguish 'never rehearsed' from 'wrong review state'); (3) on {:ok, assertion_run}, verifies assertion_run.plan_digest matches the plan_digest being applied (a STALE rehearsal against an older plan must not satisfy the gate -- use the same constant-time PromotionDigest.verify_digest/2 comparison verify_apply_digest/2 already uses, not a raw ==); on mismatch, a distinct error reason (do not conflate with the top-level digest_mismatch, which is a different check against a different pair of digests -- name it so the two are never confusable in a log or test failure message); (4) verifies assertion_run.assertions_failed == 0 (never status == :passed, per the ISSUE-FIXER diagnosis and promotions.ex's own documented gate condition) -- on failure, a distinct error reason. Design must state: the exact new @spec for apply_review_error() (add the new reason(s) as a union member, do not silently widen an existing catch-all), the exact new with-chain clause(s) and their ordering, the exact new private function signature(s) (verify_rehearsed/2 or similar -- design decides the name/shape, not a prescribed one), what changes (if anything) in R7's router handler (lib/letflow/routers/promotions.ex handle_apply/2) to map the new error reason(s) to an HTTP status/error body consistent with this module's existing 409-for-:invalid_transition / 409-for-:digest_mismatch pattern (a plausible default is another 409 with its own detail string, since this is also a state-transition-not-permitted case -- state and justify whichever status CODE-DESIGNER picks), and a plain-English worked example of the exact sequence of calls/returns for the three new failure paths (no rehearsal / stale rehearsal / failed rehearsal) plus the one success path. Design artefacts carry signatures, type shapes, and prose only -- NO implementation code (no full function bodies) per this repo's design-doc convention (see CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's own gate criteria).
acceptance_criteria: Design covers every one of ISS-0732's stated requirements: a review cannot be applied without a matching-digest, assertions_failed == 0 PromotionAssertionRun
Design distinguishes all 3 new failure modes (no rehearsal / stale-digest rehearsal / failed rehearsal) with distinct, named error reasons -- none reuses :invalid_transition or :digest_mismatch
Design states the exact new apply_review_error() @spec union
Design states the exact with-chain insertion point (after verify_approved/1, before do_apply_review/3) and ordering relative to the existing checks
Design states what R7's router handler (handle_apply/2) must do with each new error reason, with an HTTP status and justification
Design contains zero full function bodies / executable Elixir code blocks (signatures and type shapes only)
Design explicitly states the frontend piece is out of scope for this design (covered by ISS-0767 instead)
